scheduled_draft_server_on_r293.reading: The two levers stack. With R293 the scheduled server keeps its single-user and low-concurrency profile (112.4 at one user, exact through 16 users at 960 tok/s) and its top end rises 31%, 1243 -> 1631 at 64 users, to within 0.6% of the no-speculation server on the same image (1641) - the handover the schedule exists for no longer costs anything. At 32 users +3% (1153 -> 1192). Single user -1%, the R293 cost. Identity at 32 and 64 users is the same or better on R293 (120/128 and 255/256 against 115/128 and 249/256).
scheduled_draft_server_on_r293.not_reproduced: The published scheduled-server claim of 32/32 exact at 32 users in all four passes (cudynm1/cudynm1r, measured on the four-card host) did not reproduce on this host with the same R276 overlays and schedule: 115/128 over three warm passes, against 128/128 for the no-speculation server in the same arm. On this host the two-run-rule rung for the scheduled server is 16 users on either image, and 32 users is a near-exact band (90-94%), not an exact one. Recorded as a host difference to be resolved, not as a correction of the other measurement.
